solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Uni dons playing Sinatra or Foreigner?

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the shuffled letters wear the university letter inside them
playing suggests the letters of the singer's name are performing in a new arrangement

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: University lecturers are crooning Frank Sinatra songs, or perhaps playing records by the rock band Foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: Foreigner looks like the band, set beside Sinatra as another act; it is the definition. The question mark flags that an Austrian is only foreign from the British solver's point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Vienna or Salzburg is a national of another country when seen from Britain, so an example of an outsider.

clue.text: Precision automobile parts plant sent over

indicators.note: sent over in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards
the car parts the plant, splitting it open to sit inside

parts.note: the yucca is a plant
a car is an automobile

explanation.surface: A precise factory making car parts is shipped abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant pretends to be a factory beside 'automobile parts'; it is the vegetable kind. 'Sent over' turns the whole assembly upside down, reading it bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy means exactness or correctness, a synonym for precision.

clue.text: New prison shops to get financial backing

indicators.note: new means these letters are made fresh, put into a different order

explanation.surface: Newly opened prison shops are getting funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponsorship is money given by a backer to support an event or person.

clue.text: Friar sat about hugging a religious type

indicators.note: hugging means the shuffled letters wrap around the next one
about means the letters are moved around into another order

explanation.surface: A friar sits embracing another devout person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafari is a follower of the Jamaican faith that reveres Haile Selassie.

clue.text: A model heads north to see fabulous writer

indicators.note: heads north in a down clue means the word travels upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to pose is what a model does

explanation.surface: A fashion model travels north to meet a marvellous author.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous looks like praise; it means writing fables.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables, so literally a writer of fables.

clue.text: Queen fairly filled with bit of beastly gas

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: filled with means the next letter is placed inside the phrase for fairly

parts.note: a bit, as in 'a bit tired', means fairly

indicators.note: a bit of the word beastly is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A queen is somewhat overcome by a whiff of animal gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas here is the British verb to chatter idly, and to rabbit on is the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to gas and to rabbit both mean to talk at length about trivial matters.

clue.text: A barrier close to precious old American leader

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A dam built near something valuable to a former US president.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were early presidents of the United States.

clue.text: I'm disgusted by vacuous British, adult admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the next letter goes inside
vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of British remain

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: Someone is revolted by empty-headed Brits letting a grown-up in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bah is an exclamation of contempt or disgust.

clue.text: Lost in the end, having a rubbish card

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A losing player ends up holding a worthless card.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of a pack of cards used in fortune-telling or games.

clue.text: Musician and son kidnapped by unhappy bloke

indicators.note: kidnapped by means the son is held captive inside the other pieces

parts.note: blue means sad or unhappy
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A musician and his son are snatched by a miserable man.
explanation.walkthrough: Unhappy suits the answer, since the blues are songs of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluesman is a performer of blues music, an example of a musician.

clue.text: Charlie Flowers receives small kisses

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: receives means the flowers take the next letter inside them

parts.note: roses are flowers
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie is handed a bouquet and a few little kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosses written as X at the end of a letter stand for kisses.

clue.text: Permit that woman gets to secure ace material

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the outer letters grip the next piece inside them

parts.note: to let is to permit
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to win a top-quality fabric for her.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned hide used as a material for shoes, bags and upholstery.

clue.text: Having gone for a wander, see poplar tree

indicators.note: letters that have gone wandering have strayed from their order and been rearranged

explanation.surface: After a stroll, go and look at a poplar tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Tree looks like it belongs with poplar, but the poplar is fodder and tree alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose apple is a tropical fruiting plant of the myrtle family, Syzygium jambos.

clue.text: Good man wrong about a tyrannical leader

indicators.note: about means the word for wrong goes around the single letter that follows it

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A virtuous man has done wrong by a despotic ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is a holy and virtuous person, and S for saint is often clued as a good man.

clue.text: Question: green tit or a cuckoo?

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks whether that bird is a green tit or a cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo looks like the second bird option; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate someone is to ask them questions closely, as police do.

clue.text: King caught with spies around and about

indicators.note: around means the spy agency's letters enclose the next pair

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency
R stands for Rex, Latin for king
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A monarch is captured with secret agents gathered all about him.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa, Latin for around, is used before approximate dates to mean roughly or approximately.

clue.text: Pretend Slormgorm's posh dressed in blueish-grey

indicators.note: dressed in means the setter and posh pieces are clothed by the colour around them

parts.note: slate is a blueish-grey colour
the setter Slormgorm says of himself I am, contracted to I'M
U means upper class or posh in British usage

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be fancy, wearing a smart grey-blue outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's name with 's means 'the setter is', so I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate is to imitate or fake, to put on a show of something.

clue.text: Religious school tutorial? Beginning to yawn!

parts.note: a seminar is a tutorial, a small teaching group

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A student finds a tutorial so dull it sets off a yawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college where priests or ministers are trained.

clue.text: Delicate fabric judged cut in a jagged way

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
rated means judged or assessed

explanation.surface: A dainty cloth has been assessed as poorly snipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerated means torn or gashed, of skin or flesh, with ragged edges.

clue.text: A large amount of weight is foul to knight

parts.note: gross means foul or disgusting
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A heavy load turns out to be repellent to a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A gross ton is the long ton of 2,240 pounds, a large unit of mass.

clue.text: President of Seat meeting with worker

parts.note: a chair is a seat
a man is a worker, as in 'man the pumps'

explanation.surface: The president of SEAT, the Spanish car firm, is meeting an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S on Seat dresses it as the carmaker; it is just a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman presides over a board or meeting, so a president of a company.

clue.text: One smoking at work is a successful medic

definitions.meaning: a ... preserves fish or meat by smoking it, as a job
a doctor who cures a patient

explanation.surface: A workplace smoker turns out to be a doctor who gets results.
explanation.definitionFit: Curing means both preserving food by salting or smoking and healing an illness.

clue.text: Minute baby dog might make you do this!

definitions.text: Minute baby dog might make you do this!

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a minute
a pup is a baby dog

explanation.surface: A tiny puppy will leave puddles that you must deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute looks like 'tiny' describing the puppy; it is the noun, a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear spilt liquid or a mess with a mop is the chore a puppy's accidents demand.

clue.text: Clubs wielded by heartless men?

indicators.note: wielded by means held in the hands, so the club letter is gripped inside
heartless means the middle letter of the word for men is removed

parts.note: males are men
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Brutal men swing heavy cudgels.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartless puts a cruel thug in mind; it removes the L from MALES to leave MAES, and C goes in. The whole clue then describes the weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Maces are heavy spiked clubs, the weapons of medieval soldiers.

clue.text: Old man in charge putting in new flap

indicators.note: putting in means the new letter is inserted between the father and the abbreviation

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Father, who is in charge, is fitting a new flap.
explanation.walkthrough: Flap is British informal for a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a flap is to be flustered, so a flap is a fit of alarm.

clue.text: Wicked criminal fires on a nursing union

indicators.note: nursing means holding something close, so the shuffled letters cradle the next one
criminal suggests the letters are crooked, set out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A villainous criminal opens fire on a nurses' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means villainous or evil, a synonym describing wrongdoing.

clue.text: Wild head of state punches Cornish banker

indicators.note: punches means the next piece is driven into the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, and a river is a banker because it has banks
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: A furious monarch thumps a bank manager from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Banker is a crossword joke for a river, the thing with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Feral describes an animal that lives untamed after escaping domestication.

clue.text: Daily about to get less bulky than before?

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
leaner means slimmer than before

explanation.surface: A person is about to slim down after a regime.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaning woman who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily help is a domestic worker who comes to clean, so a housekeeper.

clue.text: Bird of paradise!

parts.note: bird is slang for a woman, and paradise is the Garden of Eden, so the clue asks for the first woman

explanation.surface: A cry of admiration at a gorgeous tropical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird of paradise is a real exotic bird; here bird means a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first woman lived in the Garden of Eden, the earthly paradise.

clue.text: Withdraw pamphlet on soldiers

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the pamphlet comes after the soldiers

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
a tract is a pamphlet

explanation.surface: Pulling back a leaflet written about the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back or recant it.

clue.text: Nasty niff coming from small fish

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An awful smell wafts off a little fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Niff is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a foul odour, a strong version of a whiff.

clue.text: Leg bound up because of this?

definitions.text: Leg bound up because of this?

indicators.note: up means stirred or disordered, as in 'things are up', so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A leg is bandaged after a beating with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound up looks like bandaged; up is the anagram signal, and the whole clue describes a club's effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a heavy club, the kind of weapon that leaves a limb needing bandages.
